summary: Observability and provenance tools can produce a reviewable compute-contribution statement, but none can decide whether spend is a valuable contribution. The useful feature is attributable, reproducible process metadata tied to an artifact and outcome.

items.text: MLflow Tracing automatically captures input, output, and total tokens plus estimated cost for each LLM span and aggregates them at trace level, enabling a contribution statement to cite measured model calls rather than a self-reported total.
LangSmith records token and cost breakdowns per child run, trace, project, and dashboard, and permits custom costs for tools or retrieval; this can separate model inference from other sponsored work.
OpenTelemetry's generative-AI semantic conventions define interoperable attributes for provider, model, operation, and input and output token usage, reducing dependence on one vendor's trace schema.

GitHub Actions artifact attestations create signed provenance that associates a built artifact with its repository, workflow, and commit; this binds the compute statement to the output that maintainers actually review.
OpenCost attributes Kubernetes compute and cost to namespaces, workloads, labels, and time windows, covering self-hosted inference and evaluation infrastructure that token counters do not observe.
